question: Search speed of the arch-v2 dual-perspective hidden-1024 SCReLU backend vs the production v1 h64
method: Interactive UCI, Threads 1, Hash 256, blend 100, go movetime 3000 on 4 positions x 2 rounds per net; NPS = nodes/wall. v2 net is random-weight PIENNQ02 (tree shape differs, so NPS not time-to-depth is the metric). Apple M-series, auto-vectorized scalar kernels, -C target-cpu=native.
interpretation: 4.3x per-node cost, ~1.5-2 plies at equal time. This is the expected price of a 1024-wide accumulator on auto-vectorized scalar loops; every standard-design engine at this width pays it down with hand-written SIMD kernels (AVX2 on the box, NEON on Mac), which are now the top search-side priority. Teacher relabeling is node-capped so training-side cost scales only per-position; gate games at 150ms pay the full slowdown, so the v2 net must overcome roughly 100-150 Elo of speed penalty at the gate until SIMD lands.
artifacts: generator scripts/experiments (v2 random net via exporter.write_quant_v2); probe script pattern in scripts/experiments/nps_bench.py adapted for PIENNQ02
